How Cameron County, Texas Tax Sales

Cameron County, Texas, organizes tax sales to recover unpaid property taxes and return properties to productive use. This process offers opportunities for buyers to invest while supporting the county’s revenue needs. Here’s an overview of how the tax sales work in Cameron County.

Click Here to Get Dustin Hahn’s Tax Lien and Deed FREE Mini-Course
 

1. When and Where

Tax sales are held on the first Tuesday of every month at the Cameron County Courthouse. The auction typically starts at 10:00 a.m. Make sure to arrive early to review final updates and property listings.

Check out our Auction Calendar for scheduled auctions.

2. How to Participate

Registration is required before the auction begins. Participants must present a valid driver’s license or state-issued ID.

Payments must be made immediately after a successful bid. Accepted payment methods include money orders, cashier’s checks, or personal checks payable to Linebarger Law Firm.

Note that personal checks may delay the deed filing process until the payment clears.

3. Property Research

Properties are sold “as is,” without guarantees about their condition or title status. Research each property thoroughly. Use resources from the Cameron County Tax Assessor-Collector and the appraisal district’s website.

Review property details, including market value, location, and any liens or encumbrances. Property lists are published online and in local newspapers several weeks before the auction. If possible, visit the property to assess its condition and confirm accessibility.

Click Here to Book a Call with Dustin Hahn
 

4. Redemption Rights

Former owners may reclaim their property during a redemption period by paying the purchase price plus applicable penalties and fees.

  • Non-homestead properties: 6 months for redemption.
  • Homestead or agricultural properties: Up to 2 years for redemption.

Buyers should be aware of redemption rights as they affect property ownership.

5. Post-Sale Process

Buyers receive a deed to the property after a successful bid, but this does not guarantee a clear title.

Clearing the title may require additional legal steps, such as a quiet title action, especially if unresolved liens remain.

Consulting a real estate attorney can help resolve title issues and ensure smooth property ownership.

6. Online Auctions

Cameron County offers online tax sales for added convenience. The online auction platform allows participants to bid remotely and access property details in advance. Information about online auctions can be found on the Cameron County Tax Assessor-Collector’s website.

7. Additional Considerations

  1. Understand all auction rules and registration requirements to avoid disqualification.
  2. Be prepared for additional expenses, such as legal fees, property repairs, or clearing title issues.
  3. Contact Linebarger Goggan Blair & Sampson, LLP, for specific questions regarding auction procedures and property details.
  4. Research potential liens and ensure you understand the total financial commitment before bidding.
